package_info.why_malicious: These packages are typosquats of the legitimate 'colors' library and contain obfuscated JavaScript code that steals Discord tokens and session information from the user's system, exfiltrating them to attacker-controlled endpoints.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code iterates over local storage folders for browsers and Discord, searches for Discord tokens using a regular expression, and exfiltrates any found tokens via HTTP POST to a Replit-hosted or attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing browser and Discord storage folders to extract tokens is a classic info-stealer behavior, especially when combined with obfuscation and network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate color formatting library should not access browser or Discord storage folders, nor should it perform network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software might access browser storage for backup or migration, but never in a color utility library.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code in a core library file
Access to browser and Discord storage folders
HTTP POST to external, attacker-controlled domains

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into Electron's webRequest API to intercept requests, extracts Discord tokens from the app context, and sends them to an external webhook endpoint controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting web requests and extracting tokens from the Discord/Electron context is a targeted credential theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A color utility library should not interact with Electron APIs or web requests, nor should it exfiltrate sensitive tokens.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Electron apps may use webRequest for legitimate filtering, but not for credential exfiltration.
key_indicators: Use of Electron APIs in a non-Electron library
Interception of web requests to Discord domains

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious package, which loads obfuscated code.
Malicious code iterates over browser and Discord storage folders, searching for Discord tokens using regex.
Extracted tokens are sent via HTTP POST to attacker-controlled endpoints (Replit or custom domains).
In Electron/Discord app contexts, additional code hooks into web requests to extract and exfiltrate tokens in real time.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript in core library files
Access to browser and Discord local storage folders
Regex search for Discord token patterns
HTTP POST requests to non-standard, attacker-controlled domains
Use of Electron APIs in non-Electron libraries
file_indicators: Unexpected access to browser Local Storage/leveldb folders
network_indicators: HTTP POST to pegapiranha.com or kauaudeou.space domains
Outbound requests to suspicious webhook endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for obfuscated JavaScript in npm packages, especially those typosquatting popular libraries. Flag any package that accesses browser or Discord storage folders, searches for Discord tokens, or sends HTTP POST requests to non-standard domains. Alert on use of Electron APIs in packages not intended for Electron apps. Correlate file access to Discord/browser storage with outbound network activity to known malicious endpoints.
